text:
sophie.li: quick heads-up 
We ran a mid-month sweep and found 18 small contracts where commit proration ran after a mid-cycle upgrade and accelerated revenue recognition incorrectly. Total exposure ~23,480 USD. Need to decide on JE approach and whether to include as one aggregated reversing JE or individual JEs per contract.

andreww: can you list affected contract ids and invoice refs?

sophie.li: pasted summary (brief): C-3091 INV-3091-11 overrec 2,120; C-3102 INV-3102-02 overrec 4,600; C-3110 INV-3110-01 overrec 1,980; plus 15 others small (<2k each). full sheet: https://redwood-internal.s3/finance/midmonth-proration-sweep.csv

billing-bot: billing-bot: SWEEP LOG 1891000000: proration-after-upgrade pattern detected; details uploaded.

mike.zhao: glue question 
Do we have a rule for aggregating small JE items? Last time Ops wanted >5k combined per JE to reduce posting noise.

elaine.ops: Finance prefers batching where possible. Propose single reversing JE: debit Revenue GL 4000 23,480; credit Deferred Revenue GL 2005 23,480. We'll list contract and invoice lines in JE attachment. Approve?

andreww: OK from Accounting standpoint. Add note that this is a systemic pattern; include ticket request to change proration schedule when contract quantity increases mid-cycle.

sophie.li: filing BE ticket BE-4450 to skip immediate proration on in-cycle upgrades and instead apply start-of-next-period. Assign to mike.zhao.

billing-bot: TICKET CREATED BE-4450 - Defer proration on mid-cycle upgrades. Assigned mike.zhao.

cfo_lucas: please include ARR/NRR impact in the close pack, and flag any material contracts if discovered in the sweep. Post JE before close.

elaine.ops: creating JE now JE# 1891-MID-PROR-001 (pending). Will attach sweep CSV and per-contract calc.

sophie.li: thanks all, i'll follow up with the full reconciliation and post in the close notes. :thumbsup:
